verdict_reason: The logRefusal JSDoc and the new helper behave correctly and are tested, but the query-join rule now has two homes and the return parameter still has writers outside kit.js.

todos.issue: withReturnMarker copies the rule for joining a parameter onto an href. Line 197 has `${href}${href.includes('?') ? '&' : '?'}` and appendChangeContext at line 188 has the same expression, so kit.js now holds the rule twice, three lines apart.
todos.fix: Must: one function in kit.js owns how a parameter is joined onto an href, and both appendChangeContext and withReturnMarker call it. One way: a private appendQueryParameter(href, name, value) that both use.

todos.issue: The fix for the return parameter having two owners is partial. The walk note says kit.withReturnMarker owns the return query name, and RETURN_PARAMETER at line 193 is private to kit.js, but two production writers still spell the name themselves and bypass it: partyEditHref at addresses/party-edit/edit-href.js:10 has `new URLSearchParams({ return: returnSlug })`, and addresses/controller.js:30 has `const CPH_SLUG = 'cph-number?return=addresses'`. A rename of RETURN_PARAMETER would change the reader and leave those writers sending a parameter nobody reads.
todos.fix: Must: every production link that carries a return marker is built through kit.withReturnMarker, so the parameter name appears in one module only. One way: call withReturnMarker in partyEditHref, and build the CPH link from pagePath and withReturnMarker in the addresses controller.
